earnings_release.text: EX-99.1 2 a3q26gsearningsresults.htm EX-99.1 3Q26 GS Earnings Results Exhibit 99.1 Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Results Media Relations: Tony Fratto 212-902-5400 Investor Relations: Jehan Ilahi 212-902-0300 The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. 200 West Street | New York, NY 10282 1 THIRD QUARTER 2026 EARNINGS RESULTS Goldman Sachs Reports Third Quarter Earnings Per Common Share of $ 17.01 Financial Summary Net Earnings $ in millions 3Q26 $ 5,294 3Q26 YTD $ 17,552 EPS 1 3Q26 $ 17.01 3Q26 YTD $ 55.56 Net Revenues $ in millions 3Q26 $ 18,679 3Q26 YTD $ 56,244 Annualized ROE 2 3Q26 18.7% 3Q26 YTD 20.7% Book Value Per Share 3Q26 $ 372.64 YTD Growth 4.2% NEW YORK, October 13, 2026 – The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE: GS) today reported net revenues of $ 18.68 billion and net earnings of $ 5.29 billion for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. Net revenues were $ 56.24 billion and net earnings were $ 17.55 billion for the first nine months of 2026. Diluted earnings per common share (EPS) 1 was $ 17.01 for the third quarter of 2026 compared with $ 12.25 for the third quarter of 2025 and $ 20.98 for the second quarter of 2026, and was $ 55.56 for the first nine months of 2026 compared with $ 37.33 for the first nine months of 2025. Annualized return on average common shareholders' equity (ROE) 2 was 18.7% for the third quarter of 2026 and 20.7% for the first nine months of 2026. Book value per common share increased by 1.4% during the third quarter of 2026 and by 4.2% during the first nine months of 2026 to $ 372.64 . 2 GOLDMAN SACHS REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 EARNINGS RESULTS Net Revenues Net revenues were $ 18.68 billion for the third quarter of 2026, 23% higher than the third quarter of 2025 and 8% lower than the second quarter of 2026. The increase compared with the third quarter of 2025 primarily reflected significantly higher net revenues in Global Banking & Markets. Net Revenues $ in millions 3Q26 $ 18,679 Global Banking & Markets Net revenues in Global Banking & Markets were $ 13.46 billion for the third quarter of 2026, 32% higher than the third quarter of 2025 and 13% lower than the second quarter of 2026. Investment banking fees were $ 3.22 billion, 21% higher than the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to higher net revenues in Advisory, reflecting an increase in completed mergers and acquisitions volumes, and significantly higher net revenues in Equity underwriting, primarily reflecting higher net revenues from initial public offerings and secondary offerings. Net revenues in Debt underwriting were also higher, primarily reflecting significantly higher net revenues from investment-grade activity. The firm’s Investment banking fees backlog 3 decreased compared with the end of the second quarter of 2026 and decreased slightly compared with the end of 2025. Net revenues in Fixed Income, Currency and Commodities (FICC) were $ 3.47 billion, essentially unchanged compared with the third quarter of 2025. Net revenues in FICC intermediation were lower, due to significantly lower net revenues in mortgages and credit products and lower net revenues in interest rate products, partially offset by significantly higher net revenues in currencies and commodities. Net revenues in FICC financing were higher, primarily due to higher net revenues in mortgages and structured lending. Net revenues in Equities were $ 6.44 billion, 72% higher than the third quarter of 2025, due to significantly higher net revenues in Equities financing (driven by significantly higher net revenues in prime financing and portfolio financing) and in Equities intermediation (primarily driven by significantly higher net revenues in derivatives). Net revenues in Other were $ 322 million, compared with $ 282 million for the third quarter of 2025, primarily reflecting higher net revenues in transaction banking. Global Banking & Markets $ in millions Advisory $ 1,654 Equity underwriting 666 Debt underwriting 904 Investment banking fees 3,224 FICC intermediation 2,264 FICC financing 1,207 FICC 3,471 Equities intermediation 3,076 Equities financing 3,365 Equities 6,441 Other 322 Net revenues $ 13,458 3 GOLDMAN SACHS REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 EARNINGS RESULTS Asset & Wealth Management Net revenues in Asset & Wealth Management were $ 5.05 billion for the third quarter of 2026, 14% higher than the third quarter of 2025 and 10% higher than the second quarter of 2026. The increase compared with the third quarter of 2025 reflected significantly higher Management and other fees and Incentive fees, partially offset by significantly lower net revenues in Investments and Private banking and lending. The increase in Management and other fees primarily reflected the impact of higher average assets under supervision. The increase in Incentive fees was driven by fund distributions. The decrease in Investments net revenues included net markdowns in debt investments compared with net markups in the prior year period. The decrease in Private banking and lending net revenues reflected the payment of interest on a previously impaired loan in the prior year period. Asset & Wealth Management $ in millions Management and other fees $ 3,587 Incentive fees 587 Private banking and lending 827 Investments 50 Net revenues $ 5,051 Platform Solutions Net revenues in Platform Solutions were $ 170 million for the third quarter of 2026, 72% lower than the third quarter of 2025 and 23% lower than the second quarter of 2026. The decrease compared with the third quarter of 2025 primarily reflected net markdowns related to the Apple Card loan portfolio, which was transferred to held for sale in the fourth quarter of 2025. Platform Solutions $ in millions Net revenues $ 170 Provision for Credit Losses Provision for Credit Losses $ in millions 3Q26 $ 368 Provision for credit losses was $ 368 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared with $ 339 million for the third quarter of 2025 and $ 102 million for the second quarter of 2026. Provisions for the third quarter of 2026 primarily reflected impairments related to wholesale loans. Provisions for the third quarter of 2025 primarily reflected net provisions related to the credit card portfolio, which was transferred to held for sale in the fourth quarter of 2025. 4 GOLDMAN SACHS REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 EARNINGS RESULTS Operating Expenses Operating expenses were $ 11.31 billion for the third quarter of 2026, 20% higher than the third quarter of 2025 and 3% lower than the second quarter of 2026. The firm's efficiency ratio 3 was 59.4% for the first nine months of 2026, compared with 62.1% for the first nine months of 2025. The increase in operating expenses compared with the third quarter of 2025 primarily reflected significantly higher transaction based expenses and higher compensation and benefits expenses (reflecting improved operating performance). In addition, charitable contributions to Goldman Sachs Gives (in other expenses) were significantly higher. Net provisions for litigation and regulatory proceedings were $ 23 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared with $ 131 million for the third quarter of 2025. Headcount increased 3% compared with the end of the second quarter of 2026, reflecting the timing of campus hires. Operating Expenses $ in millions 3Q26 $ 11,308 Efficiency Ratio 3Q26 YTD 59.4% Provision for Taxes Effective Tax Rate 3Q26 YTD 20.4% The effective tax rate for the first nine months of 2026 was 20.4% , up from 18.5% for the first half of 2026, primarily due to a decrease in the impact of tax benefits on the settlement of employee share-based awards. 4 Other Matters • On October 12, 2026, the Board of Directors of The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. declared a dividend of $ 5.00 per common share to be paid on December 30, 2026 to common shareholders of record on December 2, 2026. • During the quarter, the firm returned $ 4.49 billion of capital to common shareholders, including $ 3.00 billion of common share repurchases ( 2.9 million shares at an average cost of $ 1,048.73 ) and $ 1.49 billion of common stock dividends. 3 • Global core liquid assets 3 averaged $ 574 billion for the third quarter of 2026, compared with an average of $ 555 billion for the second quarter of 2026.
